curriculum.title: Puppy Pic Web App
curriculum.description: A short, cheerful HTML mini-course for kids. Build one web page, add a puppy photo, then polish it with CSS — teach, show, check, then practise.

avatar.intro_template: Welcome! Today we are making a Puppy Picture App — {{lesson_title}}.
avatar.continue_prompt: Tap Continue when you are ready to keep going.
avatar.handoff_to_practice: Now it is your turn! I cleared the example. Try it yourself.
avatar.correct_feedback: Yes! That is right — great job!
avatar.incorrect_feedback: Not quite — take another look. You can try again!

lessons.title: Build a Simple HTML Page
lessons.goal: Make a tiny web page with a title, a big heading, and one friendly line.

avatar.text: Hey friend! Want to build a web page for cute puppies? Today we start with the page skeleton HTML.

flow.title: HTML is the page skeleton
flow.body: HTML tells the browser what goes on the page. We will use: - `` — the name in the browser tab - `<h1>` — the **big** heading on the page - `<p>` — a short paragraph line

avatar.text: Remember three tags: title for the tab, h1 for the big hello, and p for a friendly sentence.

question.question: Which tag makes the BIG heading on the page?
question.explanation: The h1 tag creates the main big heading. The p tag is for a normal paragraph line.

avatar.on_ask: Quick check — which tag makes the big heading?
avatar.on_correct: Perfect! h1 is the big heading.
avatar.on_wrong: Look again — we said h1 is the big heading, not the paragraph.

retry.hint: Think of the letter H for Heading — it is the h1 tag.

code_example.code:
Puppy Picture App

A puppy page is coming soon.
code_example.description: Watch me build the starter puppy page — title, big heading, and one friendly line.
code_example.explanation: See that? The title sits in the head. The h1 and p live in the body where visitors can read them.

avatar.text: Look at the code. Spot the h1 and the p. Take a breath — then we will check what you noticed.

question.question:
The

tag adds a paragraph line of text on the page.
question.explanation: Yes — p stands for paragraph. It adds a normal line of text under the heading.

avatar.on_ask: True or false — does the p tag add a paragraph line?
avatar.on_wrong: Remember our starter page — the friendly sentence used a p tag.

retry.hint: In the demo, the line "A puppy page is coming soon" used a p tag.

question.question: Finish the starter Puppy Picture App page: put the title, h1 heading, and one p line where the comments say.
question.explanation: A complete starter page needs a title in the head, plus an h1 heading and a p paragraph in the body.

code_example.code:
Puppy Picture App

A puppy page is coming soon.
code_example.description: Here is the starter page again — same title, h1, and p we practised.
code_example.explanation: Match this pattern: DOCTYPE, html, head with title, body with h1 and p.
code_example.starterCode:
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
  <head>
    <!-- Put the page title here: Puppy App -->
    <title></title>
  </head>
  <body>
    <!-- Add your big h1 heading: Puppy Picture App -->

    <!-- Add your friendly p line: A puppy page is coming soon. -->

  </body>
</html>

avatar.before_demo: I will show the starter page one more time, then you build it.
avatar.handoff: Now it is your turn! I left you a page skeleton — fill in the title, h1, and p where the comments say.
avatar.on_correct: Perfect! You made a real HTML page — title in the head, heading and paragraph in the body.
avatar.on_wrong: Not quite yet — check that the title, h1, and p match the pattern we practised.

retry.hint: Fill the empty title with Puppy App, add an h1 for Puppy Picture App, and a p for the friendly line.

points: HTML is the skeleton of a web page
A starter page needs title, h1, and p in the right places

avatar.text: Great practice on the starter page. Coming up next: a real puppy photo on your page.
Cliffhanger time! Your page has words — the next lesson adds a puppy photo with the img tag. Subscribe to unlock it and keep building.

lessons.title: Add a Puppy Photo
lessons.goal: Show a puppy photo on the page using img, src, and alt.

avatar.text: Our page has words — now for the star: a puppy photo! Pictures use the img tag.

flow.title: Pictures use the img tag
flow.body: An image needs three important pieces: - `` — the tag that shows a picture - `src` — the web link to the photo - `alt` — short words describing the picture (helpful if the image is slow to load)

avatar.text: img shows the picture. src is the photo link. alt describes what you see.

question.question: Which tag shows a picture on the page?
question.explanation: The img tag displays an image. p and h1 are for text.

avatar.on_wrong: Text tags are p and h1. Pictures use img.

retry.hint: Think "image" — the tag starts with img.

code_example.code: Puppy Picture App
code_example.description: Watch — I keep our heading and add an img with src and alt for the puppy photo.
code_example.explanation: src holds the photo link from the internet. alt says "Two happy puppies sitting in grass" so everyone knows what the picture is.

avatar.text: Look at the img line. Find src and alt. When you spot them, tap Continue.

question.question: The src attribute is the web address (link) for the picture.
question.explanation: True — the browser uses src to load the image from that web address.

avatar.on_ask: True or false — is src the web link for the picture?
avatar.on_correct: Exactly! src is the photo link.
avatar.on_wrong: Look at the demo — src equals the long https link to the puppy photo.

retry.hint: src is where we paste the photo's web address.

question.question: What does the alt attribute do?
question.explanation: alt is a short description of the image — useful for accessibility and when the picture is slow to load.

avatar.on_ask: What does alt do on an img tag?
avatar.on_correct: Right! alt describes the picture in words.
avatar.on_wrong: alt is not about colours or headings — it describes the photo.

retry.hint: In our demo, alt said "Two happy puppies sitting in grass."

question.question: Finish the page — keep the heading and add the puppy img with src and alt where the comment says.
question.explanation: To show a photo, keep the h1 and add an img tag with the puppy src link and descriptive alt text.

code_example.code: Puppy Picture App
code_example.description: Same photo page — heading plus img with src and alt.
code_example.explanation: Keep the h1, then add the img with the puppy link and alt text.
code_example.starterCode: Puppy Picture App

regex:

avatar.before_demo: One more look at the photo page, then you build it.
avatar.handoff: Your turn! The page skeleton is ready — add the img with src and alt where the comment says.
avatar.on_correct: Fantastic! You put a real photo on the page — that is how websites show pictures.
avatar.on_wrong: Not quite — keep the h1, then add img with the puppy src and alt from the demo.

retry.hint: Add an img tag under the h1. Use the same puppy photo link and alt text from the demo.

points: src is the photo's web link
A photo page needs img with src and alt under the heading

avatar.text: Nice work practicing the puppy photo. Next we dress the page up with CSS.
Final polish next — centre the text and soften the photo corners with CSS!

lessons.title: Polish with CSS
lessons.goal: Use a style tag to centre the page and tidy the puppy photo.

avatar.text: Words and a photo — nice! Now CSS dresses the page: centre the text, bright background, and a tidy puppy picture.

flow.title: CSS dresses the page
flow.body:
CSS lives inside a `<style>` tag in the head.

We will:

- Centre the text with `text-align: center`
- Soften the photo with `border-radius`
- Set a photo `width` so it fits nicely

avatar.text: The style tag holds CSS rules. We centre the page and resize the photo so it looks neat.

question.question: Which tag holds the CSS rules on this page?
question.explanation: The style tag in the head holds CSS. img shows pictures; body and p are page content.

avatar.on_ask: Which tag holds CSS on this page?
avatar.on_wrong: CSS goes inside the style tag — not img or p.

retry.hint: We said CSS lives inside a style tag in the head.

code_example.code:
Puppy Picture App

Say hello to two happy puppies.
code_example.description: Watch the full polished app — style in the head, then heading, line, and puppy photo.
code_example.explanation: body gets centred text and a soft blue background. img gets a width and rounded corners. That is CSS dressing HTML!

avatar.text: Look inside the style tag. Find text-align and the img width. Tap Continue when you are ready.

question.question: CSS can change the size of an image.
question.explanation: True — rules like width on img can make a photo bigger or smaller.

avatar.on_ask: True or false — can CSS resize an image?
avatar.on_correct: Yes! We used width on img to size the puppy photo.
avatar.on_wrong: In the demo, img { width: 320px; } changes the photo size.

retry.hint: Look at the img rule in the style tag — it sets width.

question.question: Which CSS rule centres the text on our page?
question.explanation: text-align: center centres the text. width sizes the image; border-radius rounds corners.

avatar.on_wrong: Centring text uses text-align: center on the body.

retry.hint: The word "center" appears in the body rule we wrote.

question.question: Finish the polished Puppy Picture App — fill in the CSS and the body content where the comments say.
question.explanation: The polished app needs a style block for centred text and image sizing, plus h1, p, and img in the body.

code_example.code:
Puppy Picture App

Say hello to two happy puppies.
code_example.description: The complete polished app — same CSS and content we just learned.
code_example.explanation: Include the style block, then h1, p, and img in the body.
code_example.starterCode:
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
  <head>
    <title>Puppy App</title>
    <style>
      /* Style the body: font-family, text-align center, soft blue background */
      body {

      }

      /* Style the img: width 320px, max-width 100%, border-radius 8px */
      img {

      }
    </style>
  </head>
  <body>
    <!-- Add h1: Puppy Picture App -->

    <!-- Add p: Say hello to two happy puppies. -->

    <!-- Add img with the puppy src and alt -->

  </body>
</html>

avatar.on_correct: You finished the Puppy Picture App! HTML structure plus CSS polish — that is a real mini web app.
